text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing inconsistent client-side cancellation semantics across SDKs for streaming completions. Node + AbortController ends the stream immediately, Python sometimes raises TimeoutError but the server keeps streaming, Go cancels the context but the server keeps sending until it finishes the payload. Repro snippets below, anyone else hit this?

evans: Yep, saw similar. Node hooks AbortController -> fetch abort which usually sends TCP FIN quickly. Python (httpx/asyncio) behavior depends on whether the transport receives CancelledError; if the server-side stream loop doesn't check, it keeps producing. Go side had a missing ctx.Done() check in the send loop in an older handler.

alex: Repro (minimal):

```js
// node
const ac = new AbortController();
const s = client.stream({model: 'gpt-ish'}, {signal: ac.signal});
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 300);
for await (const chunk of s) console.log(chunk);
```

```python
# python (async)
ac = asyncio.Event()
async with client.stream(model='gpt-ish') as s:
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(s.recv(), timeout=0.3)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        # observed: transport sometimes stays open server-side
        raise
```

```go
// go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 300*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
stream, _ := client.Stream(ctx, req)
for {
    msg, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { break }
    fmt.Println(msg)
}
```

evan: Concrete root causes we should cover: SDK transport-level close vs high-level cancel semantics, server not checking context/connection state inside long-running generator, and retry layer accidentally reissuing a request after abort.

sophie: PR in flight fixing Go loop check: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pr/2345 — added ctx.Done checks and explicit transport Close on cancel. pinging @jia @mike for review :eyes:

jia: I think we should standardize expected behavior across SDKs: abort -> SDK must close underlying wire/transport and surface AbortError to user (no automatic retry). Server should stop producing within a short grace window and close its side. Proposal: add cross-SDK e2e that asserts server stopped sending after client abort + no retry attempt. Agree?

mike: +1 on standardizing. Also watch existing retry middleware: some retries are eager and will re-send if they think call failed transiently, we need to treat user-initiated abort as non-retriable.

ci-bot: PR 2345 CI: passed linux/go, flaky on python-streaming-timeout-test; created issue #987 for python transport abort behavior.

alex: Action items — Evan: open SDK ticket for Python abort propagation and a small test; Jia: add server-side idle/grace guard and integration test harness; Sophie: merge Go fix and coord SDK reviewers; Mike: audit retry middleware for abort semantics. I'll add a nightly integration that hits node/python/go abort cases.

evans: On it. Quick python sketch I'll land in the ticket:

```python
# python patch sketch
try:
    await asyncio.wait_for(s.recv(), timeout=1)
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    # ensure transport is torn down so server observes EOF
    await s.transport.close()
    raise
```

sophie: Nice. Also add a brief note in SDK docs: "client abort cancels the underlying connection; do not rely on server to finish production after abort". I'll add before beta cut. :thumbsup:

alex: Cool — thanks all. If anyone wants to pair on the python integration test, ping me.

mike: I'll review PR 2345 today and check retry middleware.

alex: filing cross-sdk ticket: https://issues.redwood.internal/RED-4521 — linking PRs and followups there.

sophie: marking this thread resolved for now, reopening if CI or integration tests show regressions. :white_check_mark:
